findings.location: design.md#Decision: Customers are merged by e-mail
findings.recommendation: The whole plan depends on "an e-mail address identifies exactly one person", which the Context section contradicts: "Business customers often share a purchasing mailbox (`orders@acme.example`) between several buyers, each with their own customer record and billing address." Failing scenario: three buyers at Acme check out with orders@acme.example; the nightly job keeps the oldest record, moves the other two buyers' orders to it and deletes their records, so their orders now carry the wrong buyer's name and billing address (app/schema.sql keeps name and billing_address on customers, not on orders). Restrict the merge key so shared mailboxes are not collapsed (e.g. e-mail plus name/billing address, or guest-only records, or a review queue for groups with differing identities), state the assumption the new key relies on, and add a spec scenario "Shared purchasing mailbox → records stay separate" with a matching test in tasks.md.
findings.title: The merge key rests on an assumption the design's own context refutes

findings.evidence: moves the others' orders to it and deletes the others.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Customers are merged by e-mail
findings.recommendation: The job hard-deletes the merged records nightly, and neither the design nor tasks.md gives a rollback, a record of which orders moved from which customer, or a staged rollout (dry run first). A wrong merge cannot be undone: the deleted record's name and billing address are gone and the orders' original customer_id is lost. Add a merge log (old id → kept id, moved order ids, the deleted row's data) or a soft delete, a dry-run mode reviewed before the first real run, and a task that verifies a merge can be reversed.
findings.title: Customer records are deleted with no way back

findings.evidence: A nightly job SHALL merge customer records that share an e-mail address into the oldest one, moving their orders to it.
findings.recommendation: The requirement says "share an e-mail address" while the design groups by "lower-cased e-mail"; the spec does not say whether `Ada@Example.org` and `ada@example.org` match, nor what happens with surrounding whitespace, with two records sharing the same created_at, or with records whose names or billing addresses differ. Only "Two records, one e-mail" and "No duplicate" are specified, so the matching rule cannot be verified. State the normalization in the requirement and add scenarios for case variants, ties on the oldest record and differing identities (see R-skeptic-1), each with a test named in task 1.1.
findings.title: The spec covers only the happy path and leaves the matching rule unstated

findings.recommendation: What Changes adds "A nightly job merges customers that share an e-mail address.", something deployed and scheduled that must be monitored and can fail half-way, yet `operations` is unticked with no reason on its line, so no operations expert reviews the scheduling, failure handling or alerting. Tick it, or keep it unticked with the reason on its line.
findings.title: A new scheduled job with the operations domain unticked and no reason

findings.evidence: - [x] personal-data — the job merges and deletes customer records
findings.recommendation: The proposal ticks personal-data because the job merges and deletes customer records, but change.yaml sets `privacy: never`, so the privacy role is disabled for this change and nobody reviews the deletion of personal data. The reason for the override is not visible in the plan; either re-enable the privacy role for this change or record why it is not needed.
findings.title: The ticked personal-data domain has no active expert
